chapter_mission: Open the Codex, make the wound understandable, and show why Torin's reading of the evidence is tempting.
chapter_turn: Ben stops dealing with a vague catastrophe and starts seeing a specific wound, at a specific place, sustained by specific human cost.

scene_plan.purpose: Let the Codex land through sensation first, so the theory arrives in the body before the room debates it.
Give Torin his strongest intellectual case, then let Sera turn the same material into the wound's real cost.
Use the alarm to wrench everyone back into motion toward a site Veraine has already touched.

relationship_turns.from: private alliance — corridor warning about Torin (Ch 8)
relationship_turns.to: shared pattern-recognition — Sera trusts Ben enough to name Gavran in the same sentence as Torin. The analogy is now between them, not in her head
active susceptibility — Ben has felt Torin's argument as correct for two seconds before catching it. Torin does not yet know this. Ben will not forget it
quietly validated — the Codex's framework reads as evidence for his 'whose cage has nicer bars' position, but the evidence is not triumph; it is one more argument he has not been asked for

exit_vector: Approach to the Brotherhood Outpost. The Force ahead leaking dark-side residue through gaps in the Weave — oil through cracked pavement. Desh on the controls; Ben braced at the doorframe. Torin leaning toward it without realising he is. The caravan is now a chase, and the chase is not a chase.
notes: The chapter should make the evidence more dangerous by making it persuasive. Sera's corridor warning needs to feel earned by what Ben almost agrees to.
